text:
Ondrej Palat was a seventh-round pick who won two Stanley Cups in Tampa Bay, and at 35 he's playing about 14 minutes a night on Long Island. The production has been light, four points in 16 games, and our numbers say a lot of that is bad luck: the Islanders have scored 5.4 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice.

He's fine at five on five: about 51% of the expected goals, roughly the team's level. With the injuries up front, his minutes have climbed by nearly two a night over his last ten games.

The caution comes from last season. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.2 wins in New Jersey, but noted his results ran well ahead of his chances, so some of that was hot shooting or goaltending. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows 60% of his shots come off the rush, and he rarely carries the puck in himself. Our range has him at 16 to 31 points over a full season. He's a depth winger now, a smart one, and some points should come back his way.
headline: Palat's points should come back
